title: Shailendra Kumar v. State of U.P. & Another
disposition: Application under s.482 Cr.P.C. dismissed; non-bailable warrant and proceedings not quashed
headnote: The offence under Section 138 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (unauthorisedly reconnecting a meter/line after disconnection) is entirely distinct from a dispute about arrears/billing, which is governed by Chapter 6 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Where a consumer's electricity was disconnected for non-payment of a revised bill and he then reconnected the line himself without following the reconnection procedure, an FIR and prosecution under Section 138 are not an abuse of process merely because a Consumer Forum had earlier set aside a different bill — that civil grievance does not touch the s.138 offence, and in any event the revised bill was neither paid nor challenged. On a s.482 application at the pre-trial stage the Court will not appreciate evidence or determine the genuineness of allegations; a prima facie s.138 case being made out, the proceedings and the non-bailable warrant (issued for non-appearance) were not quashed.

holding_units.topic: Unauthorised reconnection (s.138) is distinct from a billing/arrears dispute
holding_units.question: Does a Consumer Forum order setting aside an earlier bill bar prosecution under s.138 for unauthorised reconnection after disconnection?
holding_units.holding: No. The s.138 offence of unauthorisedly reconnecting the line after disconnection is entirely different from the arrears/billing dispute (governed by Chapter 6 of the Code); the prosecution was for the reconnection, not for non-payment. A prior consumer-forum order on a different bill does not make the criminal proceedings an abuse of process, especially as the revised bill was neither paid nor challenged. At the pre-trial stage under s.482 the Court will not appreciate evidence; a prima facie s.138 case being made out, the proceedings and the non-bailable warrant were not quashed.
holding_units.limiting_facts: Supply disconnected on 13.3.2018 for non-payment of a revised bill; on inspection (30.5.2018) the line was found reconnected by the consumer; FIR under s.138 followed, charge-sheet filed, cognizance taken, NBW issued for non-appearance.

principle_tags.application: Prosecution for unauthorised reconnection under s.138 is independent of any billing/arrears dispute under Chapter 6 of the Code; a favourable consumer-forum order on a bill does not bar the s.138 prosecution.

The inherent power under s.482 Cr.P.C. is used sparingly and not to appreciate evidence or test the genuineness of allegations at the pre-trial/summoning stage; where a prima facie offence is disclosed, the proceedings are not quashed.

not_decided.point: Guilt under s.138 and the correctness of the revised bill
not_decided.note: Left to the trial; the Court expressly declined to appreciate evidence at the pre-trial stage, and noted the revised bill had not been challenged before any competent court.
